concerns.text: The plan uses the pseudo‑Cℓ estimator with MASTER mask correction (FR‑004) to obtain dipole and quadrupole amplitudes. For a dataset with ~1500 supernovae sparsely covering the sky (many empty HEALPix pixels at Nside = 32), pseudo‑Cℓ can be biased and its error model (assuming Gaussian, isotropic noise) is not appropriate. A more robust approach would be a direct dipole/quadrupole fit (e.g., weighted least‑squares on individual supernova residuals) that properly accounts for the irregular sampling and per‑object uncertainties.

The current pipeline aggregates residuals per HEALPix pixel and then applies the pseudo‑Cℓ estimator, but it does not propagate the individual distance‑modulus uncertainties (μ_err) into the harmonic analysis. Ignoring measurement errors can lead to underestimated uncertainties on the dipole/quadrupole amplitudes and overly optimistic p‑values. The method should weight each supernova (or pixel) by the inverse variance of its residual when computing the spherical‑harmonic coefficients.
